subject: Architecture
title: Iron and Glass: The Crystal Palace Revolution
description: Learn Iron and Glass: The Crystal Palace Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: In 1851, London built a glass-and-iron exhibition hall so large it enclosed full-grown elm trees.

buildup.text: The Crystal Palace used 300,000 panes of glass and was assembled from prefabricated iron parts.

discovery.text: It was built in just nine months — a construction speed unthinkable for stone or brick.

twist.text: After the exhibition, the entire building was disassembled and moved 10 miles to a new location.

climax.text: The Crystal Palace proved that iron and glass could replace stone as primary building materials.

punchline.text: It pioneered prefab construction 170 years before IKEA.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about the Crystal Palace's construction?
options: It was carved from a single mountain of marble
It used prefabricated iron parts and glass panels
It was the first building with electric lighting
